title: Inorganic carbon and phosphate beyond water-mass mixing on the Pearl River adjacent shelf
query: Using the supplied CMOMS dissolved inorganic carbon (TIC) and phosphate (PO4), together with daily temperature, salinity, oxygen, chlorophyll and velocity for 2011-2019, determine how far summer (June-August) inorganic carbon and phosphate on the Pearl River adjacent shelf depart from conservative mixing of the water masses that meet there, and what causes the departures. Use valid ocean cells in 112-116 E, 20-23 N with water depth no greater than 200 m, and define and justify the end-member water masses from the supplied fields. Quantify where, when and by how much carbon and phosphate are removed in the surface plume and added in the bottom water, and how this differs among the nine summers. Test whether the carbon departures are matched by phosphate and oxygen in the proportions expected for the production and respiration of organic matter, and estimate how much of the bottom-water addition the production in the plume above could supply. Alkalinity, pCO2, air-sea CO2 flux, nitrate, river loads and winds are not supplied; state what this prevents you from concluding, and do not present a departure from mixing as a closed carbon budget.

region.name: Pearl River adjacent shelf, South China Sea
